description:
Found in the compiler profile of 2026-10-20 (warm compiles, all test and example modules; docs/performance.md 6.38-6.39).

After the arm_reads/2 cut (defk-o08.3), the copy analysis's next cost is the reads of each statement: Copies.enter_stmt/4 took about 4.5% of the compiler's time (SatEx.Kernels 16 of 485 ms) and live_around/4 about 1.9%. Two sources of repeated work:
- A block's statements are walked twice: live_after/1 walks each with stmt_reads/1, then enter_stmt/4 walks the same statement again with reads/1 (the rhs only, or the whole statement, for the same term).
- Nesting: reads/1 of a statement walks every statement nested in it, and each nested statement is walked again when its own block is entered, so a statement d blocks deep is walked d+1 times.

Do: walk each statement's reads once. For example, compute per block in one pass what both live_after/1 and enter_stmt/4 need (the statement's reads and its rhs reads), and pass it down; or build a statement's reads from its nested blocks' reads where the shapes allow. Keep reads/1, stmt_reads/1 and live_after/1 as the spec (property test, as copies_test does for arm_reads/2).

Measure with the harness (DEFK_COMPILE_TIME, dev/compile_time.exs --reductions, docs/agents/runs.md). Context: after defk-o08.3 the compiler is at +17.6% of its work before the symbolic-bounds chain; the ceiling is +15% (ADR-0007).

Gate: byte-identical mix dump_c against an untouched main checkout; mix ci; PR per AGENTS.md. Blocked by defk-o08.3 (same module, and it measures against that state).
title: Copy analysis: each statement's reads walked once (enter_stmt/4 and live_after/1 walk them again per level)
